checks.label: Independent biological replication
checks.note: 7 baseline and 8 case animal units are supported by primary sources. Source-replicate aliases identify the documented sampling units; unpublished animal or donor IDs are not invented. The primary manuscript identifies the RNA-seq cohort as 15 WT animals (7 chow, 8 HFD), describes male mice selected from each genotype for HFD, and terminal hypothalamus sampling. Exact GEO descriptions join all fifteen registered columns. WT source-replicate aliases denote those animals, not invented animal IDs. Group housing before the experiment is documented; the brief individual calorimetry assay is not used to claim single housing throughout the dietary study.

checks.label: Count conservation
checks.note: The configured input is normalized expression. Raw-count conservation does not apply.

checks.label: Normalization and transformation
checks.note: All 15 recorded transformation errors are at most 0.000001 and transformed expression totals match the current matrix. Independently replayed the declared numeric model with R 4.6.0, edgeR 4.10.1, limma 3.68.4; all 37,035 published DE rows agree within absolute 0.000001 + relative 0.000001 tolerance under the R 4.6.0 rules (features aggregated by their recorded public symbol before the fit, unmapped features kept in the fit, count estimates unrounded). This verifies consumption of the declared normalized input, not unpublished upstream normalization.

checks.label: Model design and input scale
checks.note: limma matches the configured matrix input. Recomputed group design rank is 2/2, with 13 residual degrees of freedom. This checks identifiability and the declared route, not every biological confounder.

checks.label: Result integrity and statistical values
checks.note: All 37,035 displayed genes are unique and trace to the current analysis table, with finite effects and probabilities in [0, 1].

checks.note: Primary-source replication review remains unresolved. Current columns join the seven exact control-animal GEO titles (3 chow, 4 HFD); the TFAM-knockout libraries are excluded. The paper describes frozen ARC micropunches from mice but Figure 1 reports two males and two females per diet, whereas the deposited chow cohort contains two males and one female. GEO age 20 weeks also differs from the paper diet-start8 weeks plus10-week exposure. The missing chow profile and cohort correspondence are unresolved; animal-like numeric labels alone do not erase these discrepancies. No unpublished cage or litter identities are inferred.
